title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir, 21 Aug to 8 Oct 2026
summary: Between 21 Aug and 8 Oct 2026 the lake went from 30.63 km2 to 29.91 km2, while the whole circle got brighter, with mean HH up 1.35 dB. The 8 Oct date carries two flags, so this brightening should not be read as change on the ground.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: Over 48 days the lake changed by -0.72 km2, or -2.4%. HH turned brighter by more than 3 dB on 20.7 km2 and darker on only 0.16 km2. HV turned brighter on 7.6 km2, and mean HV rose by 0.89 dB.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: The brightening covers every type. Rough dry ground and fields had 10.58 km2 brighter in HH and rose 2.08 dB on average, and trees, shrub and rugged slopes had 5.52 km2 brighter. Built-up land, which should stay stable, rose 1.84 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause: a processing offset in the 8 Oct product, since buildings brightened like fields; reprocessed files would settle it. Possible cause: a wet surface after rain; local rain records for early October would check it. Possible cause for the lake: slow drawdown; the dam's level records would confirm it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: 8 Oct 2026 carries two flags: the lake water threshold moved more than 1.0 dB from the previous date, and backscatter over built-up land shifted more than 0.5 dB from its June-September median. Both lower confidence in every number from that date. Lake areas are approximate: 10.4% and 8.9% of the outline falls on land in the optical photo.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Use an unflagged date for a firm lake figure, check rain records for early October, and ask NASA whether the October products will be reprocessed.
